title.en: Circular-filament vacuum field on a cylindrical grid
title.zh: 柱坐标网格上的圆电流丝真空场

summary: Evaluate ideal circular-filament fields on a uniform rectilinear R,Z grid and integrate radial flux from the first radial node. The named fields are returned in one scirel._result.Result mapping.

capability: Circular-filament vacuum field on a cylindrical grid
Evaluate ideal circular-filament fields on a uniform rectilinear R-Z grid and integrate radial flux from the first radial node.
operation: filament vacuum-field evaluation with radial flux integration
grid coordinates and filament currents -> psi, BR and BZ grids
discovery.model: Ideal circular-filament vacuum field with no near-axis cutoff.
discovery.geometry: Rectilinear grid with the radial coordinate varying along exactly one array axis.
discovery.boundary: The first radial node is the psi reference and the axis radial field is zero; source-target coincidence remains singular.

identity.relation: Filament vacuum field and radial flux integration
identity.direction: grid coordinates and filament currents to psi, BR, and BZ grids
identity.definition: Evaluate the Green kernel at grid points and integrate R*BZ with a radial trapezoid recurrence. The documented fields are returned together in a scirel._result.Result mapping; mapping and attribute access expose the same values. No nested mapping is returned.
identity.model: Ideal circular-filament vacuum field with no near-axis cutoff.
identity.geometry: Rectilinear grid with the radial coordinate varying along exactly one array axis.
identity.coordinates: R,Z in metres; filament current in amperes; psi Wb/rad; fields tesla.
identity.boundary: The first radial node is the psi reference and axis radial field is zero; source-target coincidence remains singular.
assumptions: The radial axis is nonnegative, strictly increasing, and uniformly spaced.
No 2pi factor is applied to psi.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.shape: 2-D, at least two points per axis
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative, rectilinear, uniformly spaced and strictly increasing along exactly one array axis.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.constraints: Finite and rectilinear along the other axis; axial order is not constrained.

inputs.name: filaments
inputs.description: Ideal circular source rows [R0_m, Z0_m, current_A].
inputs.constraints: Finite with strictly positive source radius; an empty source set is allowed; no source may coincide with a target grid point.

outputs.name: psi
outputs.description: Field of the returned scirel._result.Result mapping: Psi=R A_phi from radial trapezoidal integration of R times B_Z, referenced to the first radial grid point.
outputs.constraints: Zero at the first radial grid point; no 2*pi factor is applied.

outputs.name: b_r
outputs.description: Field of the returned scirel._result.Result mapping: Superposed radial magnetic field.
outputs.constraints: Zero on the cylindrical axis R=0 under the Green-kernel axis limit.

outputs.name: b_z
outputs.description: Field of the returned scirel._result.Result mapping: Superposed axial magnetic field.

preconditions: The radial axis is nonnegative, strictly increasing, and uniformly spaced.
supported: Transposed rectilinear layouts, superposition, analytic axis BZ, and radial trapezoid recurrence.
excluded: Nonrectilinear grids, finite-wire self-fields, and continuum convergence claims.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for malformed grids, nonfinite values, invalid axes, or source/target singularity.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError is raised for a nonfinite Green or integrated result.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; kernel evaluation and quadrature are direct.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No scirel._result.Result field mapping is returned after validation or arithmetic failure.

example.description: Evaluate one off-grid filament on a 4x5 rectilinear grid.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel._result import Result
from scirel.field import integrate_filament_vacuum_field
r_grid, z_grid = np.meshgrid(
    np.linspace(0.0, 0.3, 5), np.linspace(-0.2, 0.2, 4)
)
result = integrate_filament_vacuum_field(
    r_grid, z_grid, [[0.45, -0.1, 1500.0]]
)
assert isinstance(result, Result)
assert list(result) == ['psi', 'b_r', 'b_z']
assert result.psi is result['psi']
assert all(value.shape == r_grid.shape for value in result.values())
assert np.isfinite(result['b_z']).all()
np.testing.assert_array_equal(result['psi'][:, 0], 0.0)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(result['b_r'][:, 0], 0.0)
example.expected: All returned arrays have shape (4,5), psi and BR are zero on the first radial column, and BZ is finite. The returned object is a scirel._result.Result mapping; each field is also readable as an attribute.

scope: Radial quadrature increment and first-grid-point reference.

test_radial_flux_matches_psi_ra_phi_with_first_radius_reference compares radial quadrature with the maintained circular-filament psi=R A_phi response away from the source; this is a shared-kernel comparison, not an independent psi oracle.
Transposed rectilinear layout and invalid radial grid.

In tests/cross_domain/test_field_green_correction.py, test_radial_quadrature_uses_correct_unclipped_filament_field directly calls integrate at (R,Z)=(1e-10,0.2) and (0.4,1e-8), comparing b_r and b_z with a 70-digit ideal-loop expression and checking the first-column zero reference and next-column trapezoid. test_radial_quadrature_active_and_inactive_self_are_distinct checks active coincidence rejection and zero-current coincidence; test_public_field_interfaces_reject_complex_coordinates includes api=integrate.
The named result preserves the captured key order, values, shapes, dtypes, mapping access and attribute access; failures retain their exception types and messages.
verification.evidence_ceiling: tests/field/test_filament_vacuum_field.py calls integrate_filament_vacuum_field as scientific_function and by its own name. test_superposition_and_axis_boundary and test_axis_field_matches_circular_filament_analytic_limit bind superposition, the first-radius reference and the analytic axial field; test_radial_flux_preserves_left_to_right_trapezoid_recurrence covers both array orientations. The direct integrate cases in the shared file supply independent high-precision b_r/b_z comparisons at the named near-axis and near-wire points. The psi comparison uses a maintained shared kernel. Aggregate-only formula-cutover and radial near-wire separation assertions do not directly cover this wrapper. No nonrectilinear-grid, finite-wire self-field or continuum-convergence certification follows.
known_limitations: The returned flux uses the first radial grid point as reference and omits a 2-pi flux factor.

An active nonzero-current ideal source coincident with a target is singular and is rejected; a zero-current coincident source remains inactive, as asserted by test_radial_quadrature_active_and_inactive_self_are_distinct.

The bound tests directly check singularity and complex-input rejection, but do not directly assert the final nonfinite integrated-output check. That path is implemented; its direct fixture coverage is UNKNOWN.
The radial trapezoidal error in psi must be verified by grid refinement; even when the magnetic field uses the analytic relation, the discrete psi is not claimed to equal the analytic R*A_phi.
